title: Solo dev, building a Napoleonic naval career game with Claude, Suno and ElevenLabs
author: schwerergusto
selftext:
I'm a solo dev making Prize Money: Age of Sail, a single-player career game in Nelson's navy and Pirate and Privateer careers also, starting in 1800: a living chart of 130 real ports, with every action fought in 3D (this clip is Victory against Bucentaure at Trafalgar).  
I have made it as realistic as possible while balancing to still make it fun and not tedious to play.

How AI is used:

* Code: Claude writes most of it in Godot 4, with the chart as an embedded web view. I have directed, played extensively and made all the decisions based on my historical knowledge (thanks to Patrick O'Brian amongst others); it builds, tests and delivers versions to my Mac.
* Everything is data-driven: every rule and number lives in data files, each block with a short note saying what it does and why, so the AI (or I) can tune balance without digging through code.
* Testing: Myself many hours of fine tuning since inception and I get multiple bot players to run 30+ careers of 20+ years each to find exploits and balance problems. Bugs and graphical errors I have found pretty much all myself.
* Music: Suno (my theme is a humming track; tip: putting the hum in the lyrics box works better than "no vocals").
* Sound effects: ElevenLabs for guns, sea and crew, levelled by loudness so no gun sounds weak.
* Not AI: the ship models are bought a few made by Fable 5.2, or Creative Commons, and the history has been checked by hand.

Biggest lesson so far: AI is fast at building, but even the latest models need hand holding and a lot of direction. Then the tuning, score and sound (through 100's of takes) are mammoth jobs taking weeks and then play testing fixes over and over myself. Today a recording of my own playtest showed that a commission had silently vanished which then found a cascade of other minor linked issues, which of course led to a fix across the whole game. And am going through those now...!

Happy to answer questions about the workflow. It's on Epic for wishlists. Steam coming soon.

Updates and discussion: r/PrizeMoneyGame
